protocol.prompt: Hey, how are you doing today?
protocol.description: A female speaker delivers a slightly expressive and animated speech with a moderate speed and pitch. The recording is of very high quality, with the speaker's voice sounding clear and very close up.
protocol.environment: Apple M2 24 GB, macOS 15.7.3; exclusive sequential processes; desktop apps remained running; load average 2.8-5.2.
protocol.timing: Warm complete synthesis; includes T5, prefill/state seed, host embedding, prediction, row writes, logit readback, DAC. Excludes model load and cold compilation.
protocol.baseline_selection: CPU-only initial noisy run and repeat both retained. Reported CPU comparison uses repeat; all other reported configs use their first measured set.
protocol.env: CPU and Metal disable Core ML and unset strict. Hybrid and full Core ML use cpu_and_ane with strict=1 and disable unset.
protocol.percentile_note: p95 over three measured calls is descriptive only; not a tail-latency characterization.
protocol.audio_note: Greedy benchmark audio is degenerate throughput output, not a speech-quality sample.

limitations: ASR is a recognition proxy, not listening/MOS or perceptual equivalence.
Gujarati ASR is unreliable for scoring: explicit gu historically emits Devanagari; raw transcripts retained and numeric scores unavailable.
EOS/cap labels inferred; CLI has no direct EOS/stop trace or delayed decoder step field.
Finite/non-silent checks cover saved PCM16, not inaccessible preencoding float tensors.
3 seeds and 2 prompts per model do not establish duration distributions or overall speech quality; cap-censored rows limit comparisons.
Production-v2 teacher-forced CoreML quality uses f32 host; its speed tests and this free-run use q8 host. Exact q8-host teacher-forced quality is still unmeasured here. No new benchmark or export.
Old graph vs V2 sampled paths can diverge from tiny logit changes; case0 request bounds and CLI binary changed.
